A1.justification: Both PDFs describe Combinatorial Rising Bandit and CRUCB. Their complete main texts, equations, figures, tables and appendices are readable and support reliable matching despite substantial revision and reorganization.

before.justification: V1 reports original synthetic graph-task experiments and AntMaze reinforcement-learning results, including cumulative regret curves and exploration heatmaps.

after.justification: V2 reports original synthetic and AntMaze results, including additional k-MAX experiments and evaluations on smaller graph structures.

M1.justification: Algorithm 1 and Eqs. (11)–(13) retain the same initialization, recent-mean/slope estimator, confidence bonus, task-specific Solver and updates. The broader reward assumptions and new evaluations do not introduce a new CRUCB component or update rule.

E1.justification: V2 adds an evaluated k-MAX task with K=5 and k=2, extending empirical coverage to non-additive reward aggregation. V1 used k-MAX only as a theoretical counterexample. The existing shortest-path, matching, spanning-tree and AntMaze tasks remain represented.

E2.justification: The evaluated comparator set remains R-ed-UCB, SW-UCB, SW-TS, SW-CUCB and SW-CTS. These methods remain in the corresponding graph and AntMaze comparisons and are also used in the added experiments; their appendix pseudocode is retained.

E3.justification: Synthetic settings change from c=1.1 and a 200,000-round horizon in v1 to c=1.2, blockwise increments with explicit cutoffs, and 500,000-round curves for the retained large graphs in v2. Smaller-graph evaluations introduce additional configurations. The new k-MAX evaluation measures regret against the approximate constant policy selecting (1,5).

E4.justification: V2 Appendix C.2 adds a dedicated analysis across three smaller graph structures, testing whether CRUCB's advantage persists when super-arm counts are comparable to base-arm counts. This addresses whether the benefit merely reflects a large action space. The existing AntMaze non-concavity observations and exploration heatmaps are retained.

E5.justification: Both versions report synthetic results over five runs and AntMaze results over three runs, with means and 99% confidence intervals. The added synthetic plots follow the same practice; no new seed information or uncertainty-estimation procedure is reported.

E6.justification: V2 replaces the original synthetic regret curves with results under revised growth functions and horizons, and adds k-MAX and smaller-graph results. Its k-MAX findings include lower reported regret for SW-UCB/SW-TS than SW-CUCB/SW-CTS. AntMaze curves and heatmaps are retained. The revised synthetic curves are not evidence of same-setting performance gains.

T1.justification: V2 replaces the additive-only theoretical scope with assumptions on independent outcomes and mean-dependent, monotone, Lipschitz rewards, adds the constant-policy competitive-ratio theorem and proof, and revises the upper-bound argument. The unconstrained lower-bound constant changes from LT/32 to LT/16. The earlier additive optimality theorem and k-MAX counterexample are retained through renumbering and relocation.

C1.justification: V2 expands the claimed theoretical scope beyond additive rewards and makes constant-policy competitiveness an explicit contribution. It also claims that CRUCB's advantages persist when super-arm and base-arm counts are comparable. V1's priority claim of providing the first sublinear rising-bandit regret lower bound is removed.

C2.justification: V2 argues that overlapping base arms invalidate rested modeling at the super-arm level, extending v1's emphasis on inefficient exploration across many super arms. It adds explanations of k-MAX baseline rankings through exploration behavior and interprets the smaller-graph results accordingly. V1's explicit additive-reward limitation and associated future-work paragraph are removed.

D1.justification: V2 documents blockwise synthetic increment formulas and adds smaller-graph specifications to Table 1. However, v1's explicit blossom and Kruskal solver descriptions and edge-weight conversion instructions disappear. AntMaze hyperparameters, processing descriptions and the code attribution to Yoon et al. remain substantially unchanged.

R1.justification: Related work is substantially repositioned around CRB combining rested base arms with partially restless super arms, emphasizing why existing frameworks cannot simply be combined. Ortiz et al. (2019) and Patil et al. (2022) are added, while the policy-regret/non-stationary discussion and several associated citations are removed.

P1.justification: The abstract, introduction, related work, formulation and experimental narrative undergo extensive rewriting. Optimality becomes a separate section, the experimental setup is reorganized, and appendix contents are reordered. V2 also adds an impact statement.

P2.justification: V2 redraws Figure 1 with explicit parameter values, reorganizes the synthetic figures, adds a shortest-path zoom with crossover markers, and introduces k-MAX and smaller-graph displays. Matching and spanning-tree figures move to the appendix, Table 1 expands, and the document adopts a different layout. AntMaze displays are largely retained.

improvement.justification: V2 adds useful k-MAX and smaller-graph evidence and clarifies the combinatorial motivation. However, its new claim that k-MAX satisfies Theorem 3's positive lower Lipschitz bound fails when a non-maximal deterministic outcome changes without changing the maximum. The strengthened LT/16 lower-bound proof also uses an erroneous averaging denominator in Appendix A.5, Eq. (113): 16T instead of v1's 32T. These problems affect central theoretical additions, leaving the net direction uncertain despite empirical and presentation gains.
